questions.q: What is the total marks for the Qualifying Paper?
questions.exp: The paper consists of 50 objective questions worth 50 marks.

questions.q: Is there negative marking in the qualifying paper?
questions.exp: There is no negative marking, so candidates should attempt all questions.

questions.q: What is the minimum passing score required?
questions.exp: A minimum of 25 marks (50%) is required to qualify.

questions.q: The syllabus is based on which standard's level?
questions.exp: The syllabus is anchored to the 10th-standard level of the Punjab School Education Board (PSEB).

questions.q: Are the marks from this paper added to the final merit list?
opts: Yes, half the marks are added
questions.exp: This paper is strictly qualifying; marks obtained here are not added to the final merit list.

questions.q: What happens if a candidate fails to get 25 marks in this paper?
questions.exp: Failure to secure a minimum of 25 marks results in immediate disqualification.

questions.q: Which of these topics is a key focus area?
questions.exp: The exam heavily favors functional grammar over literary history.
